root.claim: A deterministic multitape Turing machine multiplies $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: Reduce the product to a convolution over the polynomial ring through a chain of representation changes, and make the transforms there cheap with two fast tape procedures that save a power of the logarithmic factor.

motivation.text: Plain transform layers cost a scan of the data at each of the log n levels, giving n log n; so both address movement and butterfly arithmetic must be made cheaper than a scan per level, and the reductions must route all transforms through those cheaper layers.

quote.quote: We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

root.salient: The saving is a strict power of the logarithm, (lg n)^(-kappa) with an astronomically small kappa, rather than a log log or log-star factor, so it refutes the n log n conjecture.

motivation.text: Each reduction turns a transform the machine cannot do cheaply into one on power-of-two axes and finally into polynomial-ring convolutions where the fast interchanges and butterfly layers apply.
